clue.text: Old book gutted young individual

indicators.note: a gutted word has had its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: an individual is one, a single person

explanation.surface: An ancient volume has been eviscerated by some youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' takes the insides out of YOUNG, leaving YG; the surface makes 'gutted' seem to describe the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Something long past and belonging to former times is old.

clue.text: Toll house?

parts.note: not a booth collecting road charges but the place where bells toll, ringing out

explanation.definitionFit: A bell tower is where church bells are hung and rung, so it houses the tolling.

clue.text: Isherwood's seeing Irving off?

definitions.meaning: a work by Christopher Isherwood, the 1939 novel set in Weimar Germany
a farewell to the songwriter Irving Berlin, as at a station send-off

explanation.walkthrough: Irving Berlin was the American songwriter; bidding him farewell gives the title of Isherwood's novel, the source for the musical Cabaret.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a famous book by the English novelist, so the possessive stands for his work.

clue.text: Pessimistic, and currently elected

parts.note: currently means at present, now
a candidate elected is in office

explanation.surface: Someone gloomy about prospects has nonetheless just won a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation with no chance of success breeds a pessimistic outlook; the term describes a hopeless case.

clue.text: British think to oust King in part of Wales

indicators.note: ousting the king means expelling his letter from the word for think

parts.note: to reckon is to think or suppose
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A British plan to depose a monarch in a Welsh region.
explanation.walkthrough: BRECON is a town in mid-Wales, giving its name to the Brecon Beacons.
explanation.definitionFit: The town and former county lie in the south of the Welsh principality.

clue.text: View of mountains destroyed in ample fire

indicators.note: destroyed signals that the letters of the two words are wrecked and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A mountain vista ruined by a great blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: A map showing height and terrain in raised form gives a picture of the mountains.

clue.text: What's brought about by persons in malice?

definitions.text: What's brought about by persons in malice?

indicators.note: brought about suggests the letters are turned around and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about what spiteful people end up causing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer too: a crime of passion is committed by people in the grip of malice or jealousy.
explanation.definitionFit: A French term for a crime committed in a fit of jealous rage, the result of malicious feeling.

clue.text: Cancel release of women from old prison

indicators.note: a release of prisoners lets them out, so the women's letter leaves the jail's name

parts.note: Newgate was the notorious former London prison

explanation.surface: Calling off the freeing of female inmates from a historic jail.
explanation.walkthrough: NEWGATE was a London prison demolished in 1904.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate is to nullify or invalidate, which is to cancel something out.

clue.text: Woman penning Volume One about godlike ruler

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as animals in a pen, so these letters go inside the woman's name

parts.note: Joan is a woman's name
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A woman writing a first volume about a deified king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing, but it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to Jove, or Jupiter, the ruler of the Roman gods.

clue.text: Rural area isn't disturbed

definitions.meaning: the backwoods, remote countryside far from towns
stays fixed in place, as a thing glued remains where it is

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means the remote countryside; the verb means remains stuck in place, undisturbed.

clue.text: Examine the conference programme? You're a fine one to comment!

definitions.meaning: check the list of speakers at a conference, seeing which people will speak

definitions.text: You're a fine one to comment!
definitions.meaning: a retort to someone criticising a fault they share

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stock retort accusing a critic of hypocrisy, and literally means checking the speakers.

clue.text: Chap following round with a petition?

definitions.meaning: the word that follows round to name a petition with signatures in a circle

explanation.walkthrough: A round robin is a petition whose signatures are written in a circle so that no one appears first.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a man's name, and it is the word coming after round for a circulated petition.

clue.text: Little growth in building material? That's about right

indicators.note: about means around, so the first pieces surround the abbreviation for right

parts.note: cement is a building material

explanation.surface: A tiny bit of development set in concrete, which seems correct.
explanation.definitionFit: An increment is a small increase, a little step of growth.

clue.text: Study reduced boy's sanity

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the word for study loses its last letter

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A truncated course of study damaged a lad's mental health.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing one's reason means losing one's sanity; the words are synonyms for a sound mind.

clue.text: Native American ruler making a complaining sound

parts.note: squaw is a dated, now offensive term for a Native American woman
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A tribal chief grumbling noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: Squawking is crying out harshly, a loud complaining noise.

clue.text: It's a complaint from some Pacific islands

parts.note: it's shortens to 's, giving just the letter S
a moan is a complaint

explanation.surface: Grumbling heard from islanders in the South Seas.
explanation.walkthrough: Samoa is a group of islands in the South Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means belonging to Samoa, an island group in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Ready in Prague to publish article on boxer's defeat

indicators.note: in an across clue, putting one piece on another places it after

parts.note: KO, a knockout, is a boxer's defeat
to run a story is to publish it
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A Czech newspaper ready to print a report of a fighter's loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is slang for cash; the koruna is the Czech currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The koruna is the money used in the Czech Republic, so it is cash, or ready money, in its capital.

clue.text: Keen expressions of disapproval raised in A &

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Keen expressions of disapproval raised in A &' is cut short: the wordplay A + rev(TUTS) + E needs a final E ('A & E'), missing from the held text, and no scan or web source gives it.
annotationWithheld.clue: Keen expressions of disapproval raised in A &

clue.text: Put down record in quantity of medicine

indicators.note: in means the record goes inside the medicine word

parts.note: a dose is a measured amount of medicine
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Logging how much medicine someone has taken.
explanation.definitionFit: To depose a ruler is to put them down, removing them from power.

clue.text: Running with heart failing shows bravery

indicators.note: the failing heart is the central letter of the word for running, which drops out

parts.note: darting means running quickly

explanation.surface: Dashing about with a weak heart is a sign of courage.
explanation.walkthrough: DARTING has seven letters; its heart is the fourth, T, which fails and goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring is boldness or courage, the quality of bravery.

clue.text: Observer's against one taking pot

parts.note: V, for versus, means against
I is the Roman numeral for one
a ewer is a jug or pot

explanation.surface: A watcher is opposed to someone taking a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A viewer is someone who watches, an onlooker.

clue.text: Unhappy artist embracing new girl

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the pieces surround the abbreviation for new

parts.note: sad means unhappy
RA, Royal Academician, is a common crossword artist

explanation.surface: A miserable painter hugging a young woman newly arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandra is a girl's name.

clue.text: Cold liquid — it's what makes a cider wet!

indicators.note: the answer's letters, rearranged, make the words that follow, so the clue is an anagram

explanation.surface: A chilled drink, explained as what dilutes a cider.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram runs backwards: the answer rearranged is 'a cider wet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Water with ice added is a chilled liquid.

clue.text: Recalled work on a city in India

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word for work is read backwards

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Remembered a job in an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Poona, now Pune, is a city in Maharashtra.
explanation.definitionFit: Poona is the older spelling of Pune, a large city in western India.

clue.text: Ray's diverted by this man turning up in the afternoon

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the time abbreviation

parts.note: PM is the abbreviation for the afternoon

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: sir is a form of address for a man

explanation.surface: A man's arrival in the afternoon sidetracks Ray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a man's name, but it is a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass prism refracts, bending a light beam from its path.

clue.text: Aspiring to provide a water supply?

definitions.text: Aspiring to provide a water supply?

parts.words: Aspiring to provide a water supply?
parts.note: a cryptic reading: meaning well, and also intending to dig a source of water

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means meaning well; read literally it suggests intending to sink a water source.

clue.text: Go back on backing some of the generals

indicators.note: backing says the hidden letters are read backwards
some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Breaking a promise by withdrawing support for the military chiefs.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Go back on', as in a promise; without 'on' it would be a mere link word, and renege means going back on one's word.
explanation.definitionFit: To renege is to break a promise or undertaking, retracting it.

clue.text: Literary pseudonym taken by a married woman

parts.note: Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A writer's pen name adopted by a wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb wrote the Essays of Elia.
explanation.definitionFit: Amelia is a woman's name.
